intent: Compare merge-base..HEAD changed files against a declared CBSP21/RPMCC24 scope manifest. Fail loud when the check cannot be performed.
reconciliation_note: v1 merges two divergent pr_scope implementations. The review-gate lineage (dedicated pr-scope CLI, ExitCode.VIOLATION, glob scope, rename handling, observed-file reconciliation, required base pin) is the base; the scan-integrated lineage contributed paths_in_scope prefixes, scope.min_coverage_percent, file_context_coverage_percent, CRITICAL uncheckable severity, and schema_version validation. diff_range.base_sha is canonical; pinned_merge_base is a deprecated alias.

severity_policy.uncheckable: CRITICAL — the review could not be performed at all
severity_policy.drift_and_mismatch: HIGH — base/head drift, observed-file or count mismatch
severity_policy.coverage_summary: HIGH when below threshold, otherwise MEDIUM
severity_policy.undeclared_dependency_change: HIGH when a downgrade or a revert-of-base-landing, otherwise MEDIUM — a per-dependency version change inside a declared package.json that the manifest does not declare

acceptance.behavior: A changed file that is declared in scope produces no contamination finding. Declaration is by fnmatch glob against files_expected_to_change or by directory prefix against paths_in_scope.
A changed file not declared in scope produces a MEDIUM contamination finding (rule pr_scope.undeclared_file).
A pinned base (diff_range.base_sha) that differs from the actual merge-base produces a HIGH base-drift finding. Comparison is on fully resolved commit SHAs, not ref strings.
When diff_range.head_sha is present and the reviewed head has moved, a HIGH head-drift finding is produced.
A manifest with no base_sha (or pinned_merge_base alias) is CRITICAL 'pr_scope.base_pin_missing'. Without a pin, drift detection would silently never run.
changed_files_exact and changed_files_count are reconciled against the real diff (HIGH on mismatch, reporting manifest_only / git_only), but never grant scope. Authorization comes only from scope.*.
Declared-scope coverage below the threshold produces the HIGH summary finding; at exactly the threshold it is MEDIUM.

scope.min_coverage_percent may raise the threshold above the 0.95 floor but never lower it — a manifest must not be able to opt itself out of the coverage criterion. An explicit operator --coverage-threshold is honoured as-is; the manifest can only raise it.
file_context_coverage_percent (declared review depth) is held to the same threshold as scope coverage; metadata.triggered_by names which metric tripped so the message is never misleading.
A clean, fully covered, correctly pinned scope produces zero findings.
Ordinary scans without a manifest remain silent (no findings).

Missing/unreadable manifest, wrong schema_version, malformed manifest fields, empty declared scope, unresolved ref or merge-base, shallow clone, missing git executable, git timeout, or failed git diff must fail loud as CRITICAL — never an empty pass, and never an exception escaping run().
Changed files and merge-base are read from real Git (-z parsing, --find-renames, UTF-8 decode). No caller may inject a synthetic diff, which would allow manufacturing a clean pass.

A per-dependency version change inside a DECLARED package.json that the manifest does not declare (not in scope.dependency_changes, not named in diff_articulation) produces rule pr_scope.undeclared_dependency_change: HIGH when the change is a downgrade or reverts a version the merge-base itself landed, MEDIUM otherwise. Motivating case: PR #296 declared a supabase bump and rode an undeclared zod ^4.4.3 -> ^3.25.76 downgrade in the same file. Metadata carries dependency, base_version, head_version, direction, reverts_base_landing.

A dependency change named in scope.dependency_changes (or in diff_articulation text) is legitimate and produces no pr_scope.undeclared_dependency_change finding. A declared supabase-only bump with zod untouched stays silent.

The sub-file dependency-direction check runs only on package.json files that ARE declared in scope. An undeclared package.json is already covered by pr_scope.undeclared_file and is not double-reported.

A package.json that cannot be parsed at merge-base or head is pr_scope.dependency_check_uncheckable (CRITICAL); any exception inside the check is caught and reported as pr_scope.dependency_check_error (CRITICAL). The check reads the real git surface (git show <ref>:<path>) and never raises out of run() — an escaping exception would abort the scan, i.e. the silent pass this check exists to prevent.
Fingerprints exclude live percentages and SHAs so the same problem keeps one identity across runs; volatile detail stays in the message and metadata.
check_pr_scope() and `pr-scope --json` report the same findings; the CLI exits ExitCode.VIOLATION when any finding is present and ExitCode.SUCCESS when clean.
